pic50-one-nanomolar.reason: Open numeric case that exercises exactly the claim end to end: the reader must express 1 nM as 1e-9 M and take the negated base-10 logarithm, giving 9. Neither the stem nor any phrasing discloses the answer; the two canonical mistakes (logging the bare nanomolar number, or using ln) give distinct wrong values, so both halves of the definition are discriminated. The key is quoted token-exactly from ChEMBL's own worked example, so the oracle is not the claim restating itself.

pic50-required-units.reason: The claim's statement is pIC50 = -log10(IC50_in_M), so the molar unit requirement is part of what it asserts, not a consequence beyond it. Answering from the claim alone, option 3 is the only defensible choice; 'none of these' is not competitive because 'molar' is listed verbatim. The stem never uses the word molar and all six options are plain lowercase unit names with no stylistic tell, so no leak shape applies. It is a strict sub-fact of pic50-one-nanomolar rather than a near-copy of it (a subject can pass this and still fail the conversion), so it is not a duplicate, though its independent evidentiary weight is correspondingly small.

pic50-transform-shape.reason: Isolates the functional form the claim asserts. From the claim alone, -log10 maps to 'the negative logarithm of the activity values'; the distractors drop the negation (5), change the base (3) or substitute other functions (1, 4), and none of them is as defensible as the key, so 'none of these' is not a live alternative. The stem asks only how pIC50 is obtained and does not name negation, logarithms or units, so the case cannot be answered from the unit fact or from the question's own wording, and the key phrase is quoted verbatim from the peer-reviewed Papadatos description.

findings: Oracle fitness and independence: adequate for a definitional claim and clearly independent of the submitted skill. The ChEMBL Interface Documentation supplies both the formula token ('-Log(molar IC50, XC50, EC50, AC50, Ki, Kd or Potency)') and the worked 1 nM -> 9 conversion; Papadatos et al. (PMC4607714), peer-reviewed and open access, supplies 'the negative logarithm of the activity values (in M units)'. Every expected answer is quoted from pinned retrieved bytes rather than composed by the planner. Two real weaknesses, both disclosed: the sources are both EMBL-EBI artefacts describing one database field, so their agreement is partial corroboration only; and neither uses the literal token pIC50, so identifying pIC50 as the IC50 instance of pChEMBL is a step the design asserts. For a standard, uncontested potency transform that step is uncontroversial, and the oracle remains fit at B.

Coverage for the proposed grade: thin but sufficient for B and honestly characterised. Three counting cases, one generated, meets the B requirement exactly with no margin. The generated case applies the whole definition; the two recognition cases decompose it into the unit half and the shape half. Only a single magnitude (1 nM) is ever converted, so the design never probes another prefix or the inverse direction, and it deliberately omits potency-interpretation cases, which would indeed reach past a claim that states only arithmetic. Three trials per case is ample for a deterministic definitional answer.

Comparison rule, tolerance and uncertainty: matched to the claim. The numeric key is the exact integer 9 scored at 1e-6, which absorbs only formatting (9 vs 9.0) and nothing substantive; the value is definitional and carries no experimental error, so no wider band is warranted and the narrow band creates no false precision. The two choice cases are scored as an exact option index. The uncertainty statement is candid about the single worked conversion, the recognition-heavy mix, the shared EMBL-EBI provenance, and the absence of spare cases.

Stronger grade: A is unreachable here and was not wrongly passed over. A demands at least five counting cases with at least two generated; this design has three and one, so it fails on both counts, and Python's recomputed ceiling agrees. The reference-side quality would otherwise support A. The design's argument that no second generated case was available is largely right: the sources carry exactly one worked conversion, and the inverse direction is that same conversion read backwards. A calculated case at another magnitude was in principle available, but the program computing it would encode the claim's own formula, which the rubric warns is not independent evidence, so declining it was defensible.

Case fit: all three cases test what the claim asserts and no more. None is a naming case (case 3 asks what the operation does, not what the field is called); none states a consequence, such as what a higher pIC50 implies about potency, that the claim never asserts; and none can be answered from the stem or option styling alone. The two recognition cases are strict sub-facts of the generated case rather than near-copies of each other, so neither is a duplicate, but their contribution is decomposition of a fact the open case already exercises, which is why the design sits at B rather than above it.
objections: The two recognition cases are strict decompositions of the generated case: any subject that converts 1 nM to 9 must already know both that the input is molar and that the operation is a negated base-10 log. They therefore add resolution (they can separate which half a failing subject got wrong) but little genuinely independent confirmation, so the effective breadth of the design is closer to one fact than three.

Cross-case disclosure risk: the stem of pic50-required-units says 'Before the negative base-10 logarithm is taken to give pIC50', which states outright the answer to pic50-transform-shape. Each case's own question is clean, so no leak verdict follows if cases are administered separately, but if the three were ever presented to one subject in a shared context the shape case would be given away. The design does not state that cases are administered in isolation.

Neither reference uses the token pIC50 for the transform; both define the general pChEMBL field. The design discloses this, and the identification is standard, but it means no quoted byte in the oracle names the exact quantity the claim's statement names.
